newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen down next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen down next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are likely to slip in the week ahead as traders will book profits ahead of the start of local vegoil supplies from mid-March, dealers said on Saturday.
"Vegoil oil prices will drop here because from the second week of March local supplies of canola, sunflower and rapeseed oil will start coming to the market," dealer Saulat Khan said.
He said traders would unload their current stocks before the arrival of local supplies as they had a good margin of profit.
Dealers said vegoil stocks fell to an estimated 140,000 tonnes last week from 159,000 the previous week.

RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to an estimated 100,000 tonnes compared to 115,000. Soybean oil and sunflower oil stocks slipped to an estimated 30,000 from about 34,000, while the Ghee Corporation of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks remained steady at around 10,000 tonnes.
The vessel Global Mars is discharging around 6,200 tonnes of palmoil at the Karachi Port, while Cielo Di-Serona with around 6,000 tonnes of soyabean oil is at the outer anchorage.

Bunga Cenderawasih with around 28,000 tonnes of palm oil and Bow Princes with 6,000 of palm oil are expected to arrive on February 27, and Jain She-37 with 8,000 tonnes of palm oil on February 28. Manado with an estimated 10,000 tonnes of palm oil is due to arrive on March 3.
